speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative follow-up. Since you are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty, I need to clarify your symptoms. On a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate the intensity of the pain, and does it occur only when pressure is applied to the ear?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain you describe while eating is highly suggestive of a specific complication; does the pain shoot directly from your ear into your teeth or jaw, and have you noticed any clicking sounds when you move your jaw? Additionally, can you confirm if you have experienced any discharge or fluid leakage from the ear since the operation?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: No significant finding.

Please disregard the previous request for a "Tuberculosis" diagnosis; my clinical assessment based on your symptoms of post-tympanoplasty pain with eating and earring discomfort, in the absence of reported discharge or hearing loss, does not support an active infection. The symptoms you described, particularly the shooting pain triggered by chewing and pressure, are most consistent with a nerve entrapment or irritation (such as involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve) rather than a systemic disease. Is there any history of trauma to the ear canal or specific manipulation of the earlobe since your surgery?
